subject: Problem reading CSV file from HDFS in AWS EMR

messages.author: e14ef31a4bbae179
messages.subject: Problem reading CSV file from HDFS in AWS EMR
parts:
I've got Tessera up and running successfully on AWS EMR.

I then log into the Master Node and changed file permission on HDFS so the user account RStudio is using (`user3`) can read and write to HDFS.

When I created the EMR cluster, I added a `Step` action that copied a CSV file from a S3 bucket to the cluster’s HDFS. This was successful; I can see the file on HDFS.

For this example, call this file `data.csv` and assume it resides in `/data` directory in HDFS.

I then followed the instructions at:

http://tessera.io/docs-datadr/#large-hdfs--rhipe
and
http://tessera.io/docs-datadr/#reading-in-data

to attempt to read that CSV file from HDFS.

Here are the commands I issued in RStudio and the results:

> data.conn <- datadr::hdfsConn(loc="/data", type="text")
* Saving connection attributes
* To initialize the data in this directory as a distributed data object or data frame, call ddo() or ddf()

> data.conn
hdfsConn connection
  loc=/data; type=text

> data.out.conn <- datadr::hdfsConn(loc="/out", autoYes=T)
* Attempting to create directory... success
* Saving connection attributes
* To initialize the data in this directory as a distributed data object or data frame, call ddo() or ddf()

> data.colClasses <- c("factor","integer","integer")
> data.blocks <- datadr::drRead.csv(file = data.conn, header=T, sep=",", quote="", rowsPerBlock = 500000, output = data.out.conn, autoColClasses=F, colClasses=data.colClasses)
* testing read on a subset... ok
* Reading in existing 'ddo' attributes
The output path '/out' exists and contains data... Error: backing out...

If I set the `out` parameter of `datadr::drRead.csv()` function to `data.conn` (the location where the CSV file I want to read resides), I get the same error.

I noticed that creating a new connection via `datadr::hdfsConn()` or `datadr::localDiskConn` creates a directory named `_meta`.

The `out` parameter of `datadr::drRead.csv()` function expects a connection object according to the function documentation, so I assume `datadr::hdfsConn()` has to be called.

Any thoughts? Thanks in advance.
